# derived from monero v0.18.5.1 source, not captured from a run
# Expectation for the doctor check `unit_no_password_in_argv` (DESIGN.md §7.1) against input/.
# How to read this file: tests/fixtures/doctor/node_layout/expect.json.
#
# _env here is FMONERO_SYSTEMD_USER_DIR rather than one of §2i's two documented overrides.
# §2i FREEZES ONLY FMONERO_PROC_ROOT AND FMONERO_SYSTEMCTL_FIXTURE, and neither lets a test point the
# doctor at a directory of unit FILES -- Systemctl::Fixture answers is-active/is-enabled/exists/MainPID
# and nothing more, while units_present, unit_loopback, unit_no_password_in_argv, unit_no_node_wants,
# wallet_dir_matches_unit and wallet_port_consistent all need to READ the two .service files. On this
# machine no agent may write into ~/.config/systemd/user (units::install refuses to run at all when
# FMONERO_STATE_DIR is set, §4.2), so a fixture of unit bytes needs SOME way in.
# THIS IS A GAP IN DESIGN.md, NOT A DECISION PHASE 0 MAY TAKE: probes.rs belongs to the Phase 2 doctor
# agent, and §2k forbids Phase 0 from touching it. Phase 0 records the gap here and in
# decisions/phase0-mock.md, and names the two resolutions the doctor agent can choose between:
#   (a) have probes.rs read the unit files from paths.systemd_user_dir and add
#       FMONERO_SYSTEMD_USER_DIR to Paths, honoured only when FMONERO_STATE_DIR is set -- the same
#       guard §2i puts on its own two overrides. This is what the `_env` key below assumes, and it is
#       one field plus one line in paths.rs.
#   (b) drive these six checks from a copy of input/ placed inside FMONERO_STATE_DIR by the harness,
#       if probes.rs happens to resolve the unit directory relative to it.
# UNTIL ONE IS CHOSEN THESE CASES CANNOT RUN, and they must then be recorded as SKIPPED rather than
# passing (§2j). The bytes in input/ are correct either way.
#
# THIS CASE: BOTH UNITS ARE CLEAN, so the check passes.
# §7.1's condition is TWO things, and the second is easy to forget: neither unit's ExecStart contains
# --password, --rpc-login, --daemon-login or a --password-file (§2b.1, §4.2), AND BOTH UNITS'
# --log-level IS 0. The node unit here carries no --log-level at all -- monerod takes it from the
# --config-file -- so the detector must treat ABSENT as satisfying the log-level half for that unit, or
# it fails on a correct machine, which is the check an agent relaxes.
# THE NODE UNIT'S CREDENTIAL IS NOT A VIOLATION AND MUST NOT BE FOUND. §2c puts
# rpc-login=fmonero:<32 hex> inside ~/.config/fmonero/monerod.conf, which the unit references with
# --config-file. A detector that greps the WHOLE unit file for the string "rpc-login", or that follows
# --config-file and greps that, reports `fail` on the correct configuration. The check is on ExecStart's
# ARGV, and the reason the token is in a file at all is that /proc/<pid>/cmdline is world-readable.
# `fixable` false, class D: §7.1's fix column is "detail names the offending flag". Rewriting a unit is
# units_present's and unit_loopback's job (class B); this check reports.
# NO SECRET IS IN THIS FIXTURE (§2b.2): the wallet unit has no credential by construction, and the node
# unit's is in a conf file this fixture does not contain.
